review.note: A7: the interval was 1998–1998 for a thirty-year conflict — the imported item's, which dates only the end — and is now the one the cited article states at revision 1376046499: "about 30 years from the late 1960s to 1998". "The late 1960s" is not a year, so the start is written as the range it names, 1967–1969, rather than as a year nobody wrote down; the end is 1998, which the article gives, with no day, because it gives none for the period itself. Nothing else on this record was touched.

title: The Troubles
summary: The English Wikipedia article "The Troubles", at revision 1376046499, opens: "The Troubles were an ethno-nationalist conflict in Northern Ireland that lasted for about 30 years from the late 1960s to 1998. Also known internationally as the Northern Ireland conflict, it began in the late 1960s and is usually deemed to have ended with the Good Friday Agreement of 1998. Although the Troubles mostly took place in Northern Ireland, at times violence spilled over into parts of the Republic of Ireland, England, and mainland Europe." That is the article's account and not yet this atlas's; nobody has read this record, and review.html is where somebody does. Wikidata item Q815436, imported by tools/import/wikidata.mjs. The item's own description reads "1960s–1990s conflict in Northern Ireland". Everything here is copied from the item's own fields and nothing in it is this atlas's account of the thing: that is still to be written, and review.html is where somebody writes it.
